transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… thanks for seeing me. I’m not sure how serious it sounds, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake this feeling—really more of a certainty—that after a commission I did, a few people in the ensemble started… quietly working against me.

It’s things like schedule changes, where people are seated, little comments in rehearsals. They’ll show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, and I get that maybe those look reasonable, but I still can’t stop thinking there’s something underneath it. I thought it might be good to talk to someone, just to see if I’m handling it the right way.
Do you think these people are actually working against you, or is it just a feeling you can't shake?

I mean… I know it may sound like “just a feeling,” and I’m trying to be fair about that. But to me it feels more like a certainty I haven’t been able to shake.

After that commission, it seemed like a few people in the ensemble started doing things—schedule changes, where people were seated, little comments during rehearsals—that sort of quietly undermined my work. They’ll show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, and I can see how those might look reasonable, but I still feel like there’s something underneath it. I’m not trying to accuse everyone, but… yes, I do think a few of them are working against me.
Do you feel like people are working against you outside of the ensemble as well?

Not really outside of that, no… or at least I try not to see it that way.

It’s mainly tied to the ensemble and what happened after that commission. That’s where I keep noticing the schedule changes, seating decisions, and little rehearsal comments that feel like they’re meant to undermine me. I know they can point to emails or notes and say there’s a normal explanation, and maybe I’m supposed to accept that, but I still feel pretty certain there’s something underneath it there.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe people in the ensemble were working against you?

I’ve tried to give them the benefit of the doubt, honestly. There are moments where I’ll tell myself, “Maybe it’s just scheduling, maybe the seating thing has some practical reason,” especially when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it.

But… if I’m being honest, for almost two years now I don’t think there’s really been a period where I fully didn’t believe it. It’s more like I can push it down for a while, or try to sound reasonable about it, but the certainty comes back—that after that commission, a few of them started quietly undermining my work through those little decisions and comments.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretation of these events might be incorrect?

Yes… I have considered that. I mean, I’m here partly because I know it sounds like I could be reading too much into things, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable.

When they show me emails or notes explaining the schedule changes or seating choices, I can see how, on paper, it looks normal. I try to tell myself that maybe the little comments in rehearsals aren’t meant the way I’m taking them.

But… for almost two years, I haven’t really been able to shake the certainty that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble started using those things to quietly undermine my work. I know that may not be the answer I’m supposed to give, but that’s honestly where I keep landing.
Are there other areas of your life, outside of the ensemble, where you have persistent thoughts or beliefs that might seem unusual or unrealistic to others?

Not really, no… I mean, I don’t think I have that kind of thing in other parts of my life.

It’s mostly this one situation with the ensemble. I know I keep coming back to it, and I don’t want to sound like I’m insisting on something irrational, but for almost two years I just haven’t been able to shake the certainty that after that commission, a few people started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to quietly undermine my work.

Outside of that, I don’t think I have other beliefs like that. Or at least none that stand out to me.
How much distress is this certainty causing you in your daily life?

It’s… not ruining my life, if that’s what you mean. I’m still working, I’m still keeping up with things, taking care of myself. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

But it does take up more energy than I’d like. Rehearsals feel more draining because I’m watching for those little decisions or comments, and with professional emails I sometimes reread them a lot, trying to figure out what’s really being said. And I’ll ask for extra clarification sometimes, probably more than I need to.

So, distressing, yes… but I haven’t lost work or stopped functioning. I hope that makes sense.
Do you think the people in the ensemble are working against you for a reason that seems unusual or hard to understand to others?

I suppose… yes, probably. I don’t think the reason would sound very convincing to other people.

It’s just that after that commission, I got this strong feeling that a few people in the ensemble didn’t like what it meant for me, or how it changed things, and then these schedule changes, seating decisions, and little rehearsal comments started seeming… pointed. Like they were quietly trying to make my work harder or make me look less solid.

I know they can show me emails or notes that explain it in a normal way, and I do understand how that sounds. I’m not trying to be difficult. But I haven’t been able to shake the certainty of it for almost two years, even when I try to talk myself out of it.
Do you think it would be possible for you to change your mind about people in the ensemble working against you?

I’d like to think so, yes. I mean, I’m here partly because I know I probably need to be more open to that possibility.

But honestly… it hasn’t been easy. For almost two years it’s felt very certain to me that after the commission, a few people started doing these small things—schedule changes, seating choices, little comments in rehearsal—that were meant to undermine my work. Even when they show me emails or notes that explain it in a normal way, I can understand that explanation, but I don’t fully… believe it, I guess.

I’m not trying to be stubborn. I do want to be fair. I just haven’t been able to make the certainty go away on my own. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had similar feelings of certainty about being undermined or plotted against in other situations or relationships outside of the ensemble?

Not really, no. At least… not in the same way.

I mean, I can be sensitive to how people phrase things sometimes, but this certainty—this feeling that people were deliberately using schedule changes, seating choices, or little rehearsal comments to undermine me—has really been about the ensemble, after the commission.

I don’t want to overstate it and make it sound like I think everyone is plotting against me in every part of my life. It’s more specific than that. It’s just that with those few people, I haven’t been able to shake it, even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain things normally. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think the reason people in the ensemble are supposedly working against you is something that most people would find hard to understand or unusual?

Yes… I think most people would probably find it unusual, or at least hard to follow.

I’m not saying it sounds perfectly logical when I say it out loud. It’s more that, after the commission, I became really sure that a few people in the ensemble were using things like schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsal to quietly undermine my work. And even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain those things, I still haven’t really been able to shake that certainty.

I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into it. I’m trying to answer honestly, though.
If someone in the ensemble were to directly tell you that they are not working against you and explain their actions in a way that makes sense, would you be able to believe them?

I think… I would want to believe them. And if their explanation made sense, I could probably say, “Yes, I understand what you’re saying.”

But if I’m being honest, that’s kind of what’s already happened a few times. People have shown me emails or notes that explain the schedule changes or seating choices in a normal way, and I can follow it intellectually. I don’t want to accuse people unfairly.

It’s just that the certainty hasn’t really gone away. For almost two years now, I’ve had this feeling that after the commission, a few people were using those things—and little comments in rehearsal—to quietly undermine my work. So… I might be able to accept their explanation on the surface, but I don’t know if I’d fully believe it right away.

I hope that’s not me sounding unreasonable. I’m trying to be honest about where I am with it.
Have you ever felt like people outside of the ensemble are watching you or talking about you behind your back?

No… not really outside the ensemble. I mean, I can get self-conscious sometimes, like anyone, and wonder if I’ve made a bad impression. But I haven’t had that same feeling that people in general are watching me or talking about me.

The thing I keep coming back to is much more specific. It’s those few people in the ensemble, after the commission, and the schedule changes, seating decisions, little rehearsal comments… things like that. I know it may sound like I’m making connections that other people wouldn’t make, but that’s where the certainty has been. Not really outside of that.
Are there any other situations or relationships in your life where you feel like people are working against you or plotting something?

No, I don’t think so. Not in other relationships, really.

It’s mostly—well, it’s really just this one situation with the ensemble. I’m here because I haven’t been able to shake this certainty that after the commission, a few people started using things like schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsal to kind of… undermine my work quietly.

I know that probably sounds like a lot, and I’m not trying to make it bigger than it is. Outside of that, I don’t usually feel like people are plotting against me. It’s just this specific group and those specific things that I keep coming back to.
Have you ever had thoughts that you were being plotted against or undermined in a situation outside of the ensemble that you couldn't shake, even if others explained it differently?

No, not really outside of the ensemble. I mean… I don’t want to make it sound like I think everyone is against me, because I don’t.

It’s been this one situation that I haven’t been able to shake. For almost two years I’ve had this certainty that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little comments in rehearsal to quietly undermine my work.

And I know they’ve shown me emails or notes that supposedly explain things in a normal way, and I can see how those explanations make sense. I’m not trying to be difficult. It’s just… the feeling doesn’t fully go away. But outside of that context, no, I haven’t really had that happen.
Have your thoughts about people in the ensemble working against you ever changed or wavered over the past two years?

It’s… wavered in the sense that I can sit there and look at an email or a note they show me and think, okay, maybe that explains the schedule change, or maybe the seating decision wasn’t meant that way.

I don’t want to sound unreasonable. I know there are ordinary explanations for some of it. But honestly, the certainty hasn’t really gone away. For almost two years I keep coming back to the same thought—that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started using those little things, the scheduling, seating, rehearsal comments, to quietly work against my music.

So yes, it shifts a little moment to moment, maybe, but underneath it… I haven’t really been able to shake it.
Do you think your beliefs about the ensemble working against you could change if you found out new information?

I’d like to think it could, yes. I mean, I don’t want to be someone who just refuses to take in new information.

When they’ve shown me emails or notes explaining a schedule change or why seating was arranged a certain way, I can sort of understand it in the moment. I can see how that might be the reasonable explanation.

But then… I don’t know, I still come back to this feeling that after the commission, a few of them started doing these small things in rehearsal and planning to quietly undermine my work. So I guess new information might help, but honestly it hasn’t really changed the certainty so far. Does that make sense?
For how long have you held this belief that people in the ensemble are working against you?

It started after I won the commission and was invited to conduct the premiere. So… about a year and nine months ago, I think.

I know that’s a long time to keep thinking about something like this. I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it is, but that’s when it really started for me.
Do you think it's possible that you could ever completely stop believing that people in the ensemble are working against you?

I mean… I hope so. I’d like to be able to completely let it go. I don’t like what it says about me that I keep coming back to it.

But if I’m being honest, right now it’s hard to imagine fully stopping. Even when they show me emails or notes that explain the schedule changes or seating decisions, part of me can accept that for a minute, but then I still feel certain that a few people started using those things—plus little rehearsal comments—to quietly undermine my work after the commission.

I know that probably sounds stubborn. I’m not trying to be. I just… haven’t been able to shake it.
Do you think there is any evidence that could completely change your mind about people in the ensemble working against you?

I want to say yes, because that seems like the reasonable answer. If there were something really clear, I’d like to think I could accept it.

But… I guess the difficult part is that they have shown me emails and notes before, about the schedule changes or the seating choices, and I can understand the explanation on paper. I can even feel a bit reassured for a while. Then I start thinking about the little comments in rehearsals, or how things happened after the commission, and I end up back at the same certainty that a few of them were quietly trying to undermine my work.

I don’t mean to sound unwilling to listen. I know that’s probably not the best answer. I just don’t know what evidence would completely change my mind at this point.
